supporting_observations.claim: Around the reported time, the proxy recorded Amy Cole browsing Zoom sign-in pages and a Google Docs document, followed shortly by Power BI pages. These records show web requests, not PowerShell execution.

The workstation made Windows Update-related proxy connections at 13:40 and 13:45, including a large download. This is compatible with patching-related activity, but does not establish that an IT patch script ran or explain the reported PowerShell window.

Before the reported time, Kerberos activity from WS-ACOLE-01 involved sean.byrne and WS-SBYRNE-01, and WS-SBYRNE-01 recorded a network logon for sean.byrne from WS-ACOLE-01's address. This is notable context but does not establish a connection to the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection on WS-ACOLE-01 was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:20 UTC, covering the reported time; therefore, the supplied evidence has no endpoint process-creation record that can confirm or characterize the PowerShell window.
Proxy and network records show some activity during the window but do not identify the local process responsible for the reported window.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually executed, and if so, its command line, parent process, user context, and purpose.
Whether the reported window was part of legitimate workstation patching or another authorized activity.
Whether the pre-alert sean.byrne authentication activity from WS-ACOLE-01 was related to the reported window.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover WS-ACOLE-01 endpoint telemetry for 13:30–14:20 UTC, if available from local event logs, EDR, PowerShell operational logs, or other independent collection.
Check WS-SBYRNE-01 and FILE-ORC-01 records for evidence of an authorized patch session or execution of the documented Patch-Workstations.ps1 workflow targeting WS-ACOLE-01 around 13:40 UTC.
Ask the user or help desk for any further details about the window, such as visible command text or whether it appeared during a known update.
unrelated_findings: WS-ACOLE-01 connected to Dropbox's desktop update service at 13:36. Dropbox is not among the approved services provided in the environment context; investigate separately. The record does not establish file upload or sharing.

WS-ACOLE-01 accessed a Google Docs document around 13:39. Google Docs is not among the approved services provided in the environment context; investigate separately. The recorded GET request does not establish document modification or data transfer out.
